prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t one objectively “best” company for everyone — the right choice depends on your home, budget and exact location in Miami-Dade. For hurricane-rated roof replacement you want a contractor who is experienced in the Miami‑Dade High Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ), installs systems that have Miami‑Dade or Florida product approval (NOA/Product Approval), and carries the proper state license and insurance.

How to pick the best Miami contractor for a hurricane‑rated roof
- Licensing and insurance
  - Verify a Florida roofing contractor license (DBPR) and ask the contractor to show it.
  - Confirm they carry general liability and workers’ comp and ask for certificates of insurance.
- Hurricane‑rated knowledge and products
  - They must install assemblies with Miami‑Dade County NOA or Florida Product Approval for HVHZ use.
  - Ask for the NOA/Product Approval numbers for the specific roof assembly/material they plan to install.
- Manufacturer certifications
  - Look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred, or similar manufacturer certifications (shows training and warranty backing).
- Experience and references
  - Ask for recent Miami‑Dade project addresses (or photos) of hurricane-rated replacements and contactable references.
- Permits and inspections
  - Contractor should obtain all permits and provide proof of final inspection/CO if required.
- Warranty and written contract
  - Get a clear written contract showing scope, materials (with product codes and NOA numbers), uplift rating, timeline, cleanup, and manufacturer & workmanship warranties.
- Installation specifics to confirm
  - Proper deck attachment, fastener type & pattern, secondary water barrier, continuous roof‑to‑wall connections, flashing details and drip edges rated for high wind.
- Red flags to avoid
  - Unlicensed crews, “storm chaser” companies without local presence, large cash‑only demands, very low bids with pressure to sign immediately.

Where to verify credentials and approvals
- Florida DBPR license lookup (verify contractor license).
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control / NOA search (verify material/assembly approvals).
- Better Business Bureau, Google/Yelp reviews and local homeowner groups for reputation.

If you want, I can:
- Find and shortlist top-rated hurricane‑roof replacement contractors in your immediate area if you give me your ZIP code (I’ll include license checks and what to ask each one), or
- Draft a short checklist/email you can send to contractors to get comparable bids.

Which would you prefer?
